GENERAL TERMS & CONDITIONS a) Weekly Food MENU for Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner is provided in ANNEXURE-I. b) Each meal is comprised of (1) common items (which are same for all days) and (2) Spe cial items (different for different days). c) Bidders need to quote only three rates (irrespective of days), for Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner. d) All quoted rates should be quoted in INR (₹) inclusive of GST and all other charges. e) With the approval of the Hostel Advisory Committee, the Agency will be allowed to sell other quality food items at approved rates and standard packet food items at MRP or les s. f) The Agency needs to execute a service AGREEMENT (in duplicate) within 7 days from t he date of acceptance of the Work Order at their own cost and expenses on a non-judici al stamp paper valued not less than ₹50.00 signed jointly by the representative of the A gency and the Institute. g) The tenure of the Agreement will be for three years from the date of execution of the A greement. j) The Agency shall comply with all laws in force from time to time that apply to its oper ations and staff, including: the Code on Wages, 2019; the Industrial Relations Code, 20 20; the Code on Social Security, 2020; the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Co nditions Code, 2020, including the Central and State rules made under them; the Incom e-tax Act, 2025 and the Income-tax Rules, 2026; the Goods and Services Tax laws; and the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the regulations made under it. MESS RELATED TERMS a) The Agency shall not engage the services of any sub-agency or transfer the contract t o any other person. If it is found at any time that the agency is unable to provide the ca nteen services and has sub-contacted to any other party, the Institute has the right to t erminate the contract and to forfeit the performance bank guarantee after giving one month's notice. b) Engagement of the required number of staff, providing uniforms, etc. shall be done by the Agency with the approval of the Hostel Advisory Committee. The workers should al ways use hand gloves and caps while working (hair found in food is not acceptable). Th e Agency should provide a minimum of two pairs of uniforms to its staff and ensure tha t staff report for duty in clean uniforms. c) Weekly Food MENU for Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner is provided in ANNEXURE-I. Extra items may be prepared by the Agency whose price may be set by the Agency aft er agreement with the Mess Committee. d) The Agency need to install vending machines or include night canteen facilities (which ever is deemed suitable by the Agency), on direct payment basis, alongside the other s pecified mess cooking items, as outlined in the tender document. e) The Agency shall, at their cost, maintain adequate stock of food grain, and groceries. The Agency shall be responsible for the proper hygienic storage of all raw materials. f) No food cooked in the mess may be taken out of the hostel premises without prior per mission of the Mess Committee of the concerned hostel. g) Vegetarian and Non-Vegetarian food should be cooked, stored, and served separately. h) There will be review meetings, at least once in a semester, among the Agency, the Ho tel Advisory Committee and the Mess Committees. This meeting shall be attended by t he owner himself or a senior representative, who is authorized to make policy & monet ary decisions. i) Suitable fines will be imposed for damage to the civil and electrical infrastructure in th e mess area by the Agency people. Strict actions/fines as necessary will be taken for vi olations related to unauthorised entry, alcohol, and banned items within the hostel pre mises. j) The Agency shall provide water jugs at each table prior to meal time, and refill them r egularly during meal time. 4. ISSUES RELATED TO HEALTH AND HYGIENE IN THE MESS AND THE KITCHEN a) Cleaning of the kitchen will be the sole responsibility of the Agency. b) Cleaning utensils, cutlery, crockery, kitchen equipments, is also the responsibility of t he Agency. c) All possible measures must be taken to ensure hygiene in the kitchen and mess. Thes e include the provision of ample liquid soap for handwashing at the basin, clean towels to clean hands, hand gloves for mess workers who handle items like salad, Pani puri, et c., head caps for mess workers, and other measures as advised by the Hotel Advisory C

ommittee. d) The Agency shall procure food articles and vegetables of good quality to the satisfacti on of the respective mess committees. e) Perishable items like meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products shall be stored in chilly ( 5◦C) temperatures. f) Spices, ketchup, and other jarred/bottled ingredients must be of adequate quality and sealed when not in use. g) The raw materials and cooked food shall be stored separately to prevent contaminatio n. h) The food shall be cooked, stored, and served under hygienic conditions. The Agency s hall ensure that only freshly cooked food is served and the stale is not recycled. Stale f ood shall be removed from Mess premises as soon as possible and latest within 10 hou rs of its preparation. Un-refrigerated cooked food, not consumed within four hours in su mmer months and six hours in winter months, shall deemed to be stale and unfit for co nsumption. Here, "summer months" means March to October and "winter months" me ans November to February. i) The food shall be neither too spicy nor too oily. The food preparation shall be wholeso me and generally cater to the students' tastes. j) The oil that remains from deep frying at the end of the day shall be destroyed and sha ll not be allowed to be recycled for the purpose of cooking again. k) Vegetable shortening (artificially hydrogenated vegetable oil) should not be used for fr ying. l) Spices must be verified to be free of adulterates. m) Salt used must be iodized. n) The food shall be cooked and served in clean utensils and no laxity shall be permitted in this regard. The utensils shall have to be maintained sparkling clean at all times. Tre y shall be sterilized each morning before serving any items. o) The Agency shall always pay special attention to maintaining the kitchen in a neat an d tidy condition. For this purpose, the kitchen shall be cleaned thoroughly after a specif ic time duration (say, 3 hours) regularly. p) The Agency shall ensure that only hot foods are served in the mess. q) The Agency shall ensure that sufficient manpower is deployed for cooking and serving food including cleaning, washing, and overall upkeep of kitchen assets and premises. T he Agency shall submit medically fit certificates of all the deployed manpower engaged in the messes. r) The Agency shall ensure that the workers are wearing clean clothes/ aprons while coo king and serving food in the messes. s) The Agency shall ensure that enough precaution has been taken to avoid rodents, coc kroaches, etc. in the messes. t) Sanitary practices like proper hand-washing before/after handling food, cleaning work , and after using restrooms, must be adhered to. u) The Agency shall ensure workers’ pay special attention to any equipment coming into contact with uncooked poultry. Such equipment shall be thoroughly sterilized through high heat and rinsed clean before being allowed to come into any non-contaminated pe rsonnel or equipment. This includes thorough hand-washing for all involved personnel a s well. v) The weekly menu in Annexure-I is fixed for a four-week cycle. A change needs the Mess Com mittee's written approval at least 7 days in advance. An emergency change (for example, due to a supply shortage) is allowed only with the Mess Committee's written approval, with the rea son stated in writing. w) Hot food shall be held at or above 60°C. Chilled items shall be held at or below 5°C.

RULES PERTAINING TO THE DAILY FUNCTIONING OF THE MESS 1. TIMING FOR THE MESS Actual timing will depend upon the decision of the Mess Committee and the Agency would be obliged to adhere to the Committee's instruction regarding it. Following is a tentative timing. Meal Timing Breakfast 8:00 AM to 11:15 AM Lunch 12:30 Noon to 2:30 PM Dinner 7:15 PM to 10:15 PM 2. GENERAL STRUCTURE OF THE MENU The following is the general structure of the menu. The detailed menu and minimum portion si ze is provided in Annexure-I. Everyone who avails food from the Mess during Lunch and Dinner can opt for one of the three categories: • Veg (V): Always available during Lunch and Dinner on All Days. Includes a special Veg di sh (as per the menu) along with the common item. • Non-Veg (NV): Always available during Lunch and Dinner on All Days. Includes a special Non-Veg dish (as per the menu) along with the common item. i) The price of both will be set by the Mess Committee after discussion with the Agency. ii) The Bidder shall specify the meal prices for the meal (e.g., breakfast, lunch, dinner) as a whole only. a) BREAKFAST (All Days) i) Adequate Tea or Coffee or Milk (200ml) + Bournvita ii) Adequate Toasted Brown Bread and Normal Bread with Butter, Jam, and Ketchup iii) Roti with Sabzi (without potato) iv) Egg/Fruits/Sprouts/Paneer Bhurji. Note, Boiled Egg (= 1 item worth), Omlette (= 1 item worth), Egg Bhurji (100ml = 1 item worth), Banana/Guava/Watermelon (1 banana = 1 ite m worth), fruits other than banana/Guava/Watermelon (150g = 2 item worth), Sprouts (1 00ml = 1 items worth) paneer bhurji (100ml = 2 items worth). The Agency is supposed to serve 2 items worth of either egg /fruit/paneer bhurji. b) LUNCH (Weekends and Holidays) and Dinner (All Days) i) Unlimited plain Rice OR any other special rice items as mentioned in the menu (eg. Bir yani, Fried Rice, Jeera Rice, Curd Rice, etc.) on all 7 days. ii) Unlimited Chapati OR any other special roti alternative as mentioned in the menu (eg. Paratha, Aloo Paratha, Bhature, etc.) with and without Butter on all 7 days iii) Adequate Dal OR any other special Dal alternative as mentioned in the menu (eg. Dal

Makhani, Dal Tadka, etc.) iv) One unlimited vegetable curry OR One unlimited dry vegetable as mentioned in the m enu. For example: if Onion Fry S abji is served as a dry vegetable and a total of 5 kg of raw material is used, at most 1 kg of it may be Aloo and the remaining 4 kg shall be Onion. v) One special Non-Veg dish (eg. Either tomato/onion must be there in the salad. It will also contain any two of the following in every meal: cucumbers, beetroots, carrots, and radish e xcept when Groundnut, Corn, Sprouts, Minced or Cabbage Salad is being served. The choic e of salads is complete with the Mess Committee. b) Mouth freshener (Fennel seeds and sugar) and Pickle to be provided with every meal. c) The composition of a vegetable item should be exactly as specified by the Mess Committ ee.
